correctness.rationale: At each of the seven rational points the tangent must be one of three incident F2 lines. All 3^7 assignments produce 24 bijections. Independent bit-matrix first-jet evaluation confirms ranks 10,15,21,21 in degrees 3,4,5,6, respectively; the key quintic injectivity is also proved geometrically by intersection multiplicities on the seven Fano lines, and the sextic kernel has dimension 7. The independent checker solved every tangent linear system and used exact algebraic-closure Jacobian Gröbner unit-ideal tests on all three affine charts for all 24 quartic, 24 quintic and 128 sextic lifts of one matching. Results: all 24 quartics smooth, no quintics smooth, 127 smooth sextic lifts. Independently generated GL3(F2) substitutions show all 24 matchings in one orbit, with smooth sextic forms splitting into 1 orbit of length24 and 18 of length168. Finite enumeration is exhaustive because the matching action and the complete 2^7 coset were proved; chart Gröbner unit ideals test *geometric* smoothness, not only rational points.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A broad genus-six classification could dominate parts of the degree-five negative case, and generic jet interpolation gives existence of polynomial solutions, but not geometric smoothness and PGL3 orbit counts across 4–6. The sextic orbit census is outside genus six.

evidence: The first-jet map has rank 21 in degrees five and six, supplying candidate equations but not their geometric smoothness.
Exact Jacobian ideal checks remove all 24 quintic candidates and precisely one of 128 sextic lifts per matching.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: General interpolation and broad curve census methods do not logically entail the reported counts as immediate corollaries. The decisive polynomial/singularity and finite symmetry calculations provide the new exact evaluation.

evidence: Tangent-filling conditions concern all rational points lying on tangent lines to some curve points; this is not a bijection of the seven curve points onto the seven dual rational lines.
The assessed constraint forces C(F2)=P2(F2), injective Gauss restriction, and geometric smoothness simultaneously.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A tangent-filling curve need not pass through all F2 points or have distinct tangent images; a curve with seven rational points need not have bijective tangents. The reviewed special incidence-plus-jet condition is strictly more restrictive and has its own exact count.

originality.rationale: The primary tangent-filling literature studies covering of rational points by tangent lines and jet interpolation, and an existing genus-six census considers quintics over F2. Neither directly supplies the simultaneous smooth rational-Gauss bijection classification across degrees four through six or the sextic orbit census. Qualified originality applies to the combined assertion; the finite incidence and jet methods are established.
residual_risks: An exact genus-ten sextic or finite-projective-plane Gauss-map database might already contain the 3048 cases or nineteen orbits under different indexing.

value.rationale: The full rational projective plane over F2 is a natural finite-geometry configuration. Asking when a smooth plane curve can make its seven rational point tangents a permutation of the seven lines is a genuine arithmetic-incidence constraint. The exact three-degree census, nonmonotone existence gap at degree five, and precise PGL3 orbit structure give a naturally motivated finite classification rather than isolated example hunting.

limitations: Geometric smoothness over an algebraic closure is essential; checking only seven F2 points would be invalid.
Plane equations rather than abstract curve isomorphism classes; only degrees 4–6 and F2.
